schemeName: Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana – National Urban Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NULM)
department: Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs (MoHUA)
targetGroup: Urban Poor, Street Vendors, Self-Help Groups, Women
occupationEligible: Urban Poor, SHG Members, Street Vendors
eligibility: Urban poor identified via SECC/ULB lists; SHGs and community groups; implemented via Municipal Corporation
otherEligibilityCriteria: Must be resident of urban area; identified by Urban Local Body
benefits: Community event & training funding; SHG support; skill training + placement; urban street vendor support; credit access
allBenefitsDescription: Provides funding for community events and training programs, supports self-help groups (SHGs), offers skill training with placement assistance, and supports urban street vendors with livelihood options.
benefitAmount: Varies by component (subsidy, loan, training support)
importantDocuments: Aadhaar Card, BPL/SECC Certificate, Bank Passbook
requiredDocuments: Aadhaar Card, Address Proof, BPL Certificate, Photograph, Bank Account Details
remarks: Implemented via Municipal Corporations. Also covers green jobs (waste management, recycling).

schemeName: PM SVANidhi – PM Street Vendor's AtmaNirbhar Nidhi
department: Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs (MoHUA) / Department of Financial Services
targetGroup: Urban Street Vendors, Hawkers, Thelewalas
eligibility: Street vendors in urban areas who were vending on/before 24 March 2020; must have vending certificate/ID or Letter of Recommendation from ULB/TVC
otherEligibilityCriteria: Applicable only in States/UTs that have notified rules under Street Vendors Act 2014
benefits: Collateral-free working capital loan; interest subsidy 7% p.a.; digital transaction cashback up to ₹100/month; capacity building
allBenefitsDescription: Provides working capital loans: ₹15,000 (1st tranche), ₹25,000 (2nd tranche), up to ₹50,000 (3rd tranche). Interest subsidy of 7% p.a. credited quarterly via DBT. Cashback for digital transactions. Extended till March 2030.
benefitFrequency: One-time loan per tranche; renewed on repayment
importantDocuments: Aadhaar Card, Vending Certificate / ULB ID / Letter of Recommendation
requiredDocuments: Aadhaar Card, Vending Certificate or ID issued by ULB, Bank Account Details, Mobile Number
remarks: Loan restructured in August 2025. Scheme active till March 2030. No collateral required.

schemeName: National Urban Digital Mission (NUDM)
department: Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs / MeitY
targetGroup: Urban Residents, ULBs, City Administrations
eligibility: Implemented by Urban Local Bodies (ULBs); targets digitally underserved urban populations
otherEligibilityCriteria: Implementation-level scheme; individual citizens benefit via ULB-delivered services
benefits: Digital infrastructure for cities; citizen service platforms; funding for tech-enabled civic services
allBenefitsDescription: Creates digital infrastructure for urban governance, provides citizen service delivery platforms, funds technology-enabled civic services, and supports smart city governance solutions.
requiredDocuments: ULB registration, Government authorization letters
remarks: Policy/infrastructure scheme; benefits citizens indirectly via digital public services.

schemeName: Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY 4.0)
department: Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE) / NSDC
targetGroup: Unemployed Youth, School/College Dropouts, Job Seekers
eligibility: Indian citizen aged 15–45 years; unemployed or seeking skill upgrade; school/college dropout or graduate
otherEligibilityCriteria: Must not be currently employed; Aadhaar-linked bank account required; 10th pass preferred for most courses
benefits: Free skill training; nationally recognized NSQF certification; placement assistance; ₹8,000 stipend during training
allBenefitsDescription: Provides free short-term skill training in industry-relevant job roles under NSQF framework. Includes certification, placement support, and a training stipend of ₹8,000. Covers sectors like IT, healthcare, retail, construction, etc.
applicationMode: Online (skillindiadigital.gov.in / pmkvyofficial.org) / Offline via PMKVY Training Centres
requiredDocuments: Aadhaar Card, Educational Mark Sheets, Bank Account Details, Passport-size Photo, Residence Proof
remarks: PMKVY 4.0 runs 2022–2026. Age limit up to 49 years for some specialized courses.

schemeName: National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme (NAPS)
department: Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE)
targetGroup: Youth (14–21 years), Graduates, Diploma Holders
eligibility: Minimum 8th pass; apprenticeship through registered establishments; age 14–21 years
otherEligibilityCriteria: Must register on Apprenticeship India portal; both apprentice and employer need to register
benefits: Government reimburses 25% of stipend (max ₹1,500/month) to employer; practical on-the-job training; NATS certification
allBenefitsDescription: Government shares stipend cost: 25% or ₹1,500/month per apprentice (whichever is less) reimbursed to employer. Apprentices receive practical training and nationally recognized certificates.
requiredDocuments: Aadhaar Card, Educational Certificates, Bank Account Details, Photograph
remarks: Incentivizes industry to hire apprentices. Both employer and apprentice must register on the portal.

schemeName: Ayushman Bharat – Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (PM-JAY)
department: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare / National Health Authority
targetGroup: BPL Families, Rural/Urban Poor, SECC-listed households
eligibility: Low-income families identified in SECC 2011 database; approximately 50 crore beneficiaries; includes all family members
otherEligibilityCriteria: Beneficiary must be listed in PM-JAY database; Ayushman card required for hospital use
benefits: ₹5 lakh health insurance per family per year; cashless treatment at empanelled hospitals; covers pre/post hospitalization; secondary and tertiary care
allBenefitsDescription: Provides ₹5 lakh health coverage per family per year at empanelled government and private hospitals. Covers 1,500+ medical procedures, pre and post-hospitalization expenses, and daycare surgeries. Fully cashless and paperless.
benefitAmount: Up to ₹5,00,000 per family per year
applicationMode: Online (pmjay.gov.in) / Offline via Common Service Centres / Hospital
importantDocuments: Aadhaar Card, Ration Card, Ayushman Card
requiredDocuments: Aadhaar Card, Ration Card, SECC verification, Photograph
remarks: One of the world's largest health insurance programs. Ayushman card can be generated at CSCs or via Ayushman app.

schemeName: Mission Vatsalya (Child Welfare & Protection)
department: Ministry of Women and Child Development
beneficiaryType: Children in Need of Care and Protection
targetGroup: Orphaned/Destitute Children, Children in difficult circumstances
eligibility: Children in need of care and protection; orphaned, destitute, or runaway children; children from conflict/disaster
otherEligibilityCriteria: Referred via Child Welfare Committees (CWC) or Juvenile Justice Boards
benefits: Child protection services; funding for Child Care Institutions (CCIs); foster care support; sponsorship; awareness programs; aftercare services
allBenefitsDescription: Provides institutional and non-institutional child care services. Supports CCIs with funds. Covers foster care, adoption, sponsorship, and aftercare for children aging out of institutions.
applicationMode: Offline (via Child Welfare Committee / District Administration)
requiredDocuments: CWC referral, Birth Certificate, Medical Records (if any)
remarks: Merged scheme covering child protection, CCIs, foster care, and sponsorship under one umbrella.

schemeName: Sub-Mission on Agricultural Extension (SMAE)
department: Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare (ATMA)
targetGroup: Farmers, Farmer Producer Organisations, Agriculture Extension Workers
occupationEligible: Farmers, FPOs, Krishi Vigyan Kendras, Extension Agencies
eligibility: Farmers, FPOs, and extension agencies; institutions running Krishi Melas, farmer workshops, and demonstration programs
otherEligibilityCriteria: Projects submitted through ATMA / state agriculture departments
benefits: Funding for farmer awareness programs; demonstration events; Krishi Melas; training camps; agricultural extension activities
allBenefitsDescription: Provides financial support for organizing farmer awareness programs, demonstration events, Krishi Melas, and training camps. Supports Farmer Field Schools and exposure visits.
requiredDocuments: Farmer ID, Land Records, Bank Account, Aadhaar
remarks: Implemented through Agricultural Technology Management Agency (ATMA) at district level.

schemeName: Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana (RKVY-RAFTAAR)
department: Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
targetGroup: Farmers, Agri Entrepreneurs, State Agriculture Depts, Startups
occupationEligible: Farmers, Agri Startups, FPOs, State Governments
eligibility: State governments, agricultural institutions, agri-startups, and innovators in agriculture sector
otherEligibilityCriteria: RAFTAAR component specifically for startups (agri-preneurs); incubation and innovation funding available
benefits: Financial support for agri projects; startup & innovation funding; pilot projects; agri-infrastructure development
allBenefitsDescription: Flexible block grant to states for agriculture development. RAFTAAR component funds agri-startups with up to ₹25 lakh seed funding. Covers innovation events, pilot projects, value chain development.
benefitAmount: Up to ₹25 lakh (startup/innovation component); state-level grants vary
applicationMode: Offline (via State Agriculture Dept) / Online for startups via RKVY portal
importantDocuments: Project Proposal, Land Records, Business Plan (for startups)
requiredDocuments: Project Proposal, Aadhaar, PAN, Business Registration (for startups)
remarks: RAFTAAR = Remunerative Approaches for Agriculture and Allied sector Rejuvenation. Incubation support for agri-startups.

schemeName: MPLADS – Members of Parliament Local Area Development Scheme
department: Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI)
targetGroup: Rural and Urban Residents, Local Communities
eligibility: Projects proposed by MP for local area development; executed by District Authority; works for public use
otherEligibilityCriteria: Projects must be durable and for public benefit; proposal routed through respective MP's office
benefits: ₹5 crore per MP per year for local development; parks, community halls, public assets, roads, schools, water supply
allBenefitsDescription: Each MP can recommend works worth ₹5 crore annually for their constituency. Covers construction of community halls, roads, water supply, parks, schools, and other public infrastructure.
importantDocuments: Project proposal, Land clearance, NOC from local body
requiredDocuments: Project Proposal, Technical Estimate, Land Documents, NOC
remarks: Works executed by District Authority/Local Body. Not a direct individual benefit scheme.

schemeName: MLALADS – MLA Local Area Development Scheme
department: State Legislature / State Finance Department
targetGroup: Constituency residents, Local Communities
eligibility: Projects proposed by MLA for constituency development; works of public utility
otherEligibilityCriteria: Varies by state; Maharashtra MLA gets approx ₹3 crore/year
benefits: Funding for community halls, small infrastructure, event spaces, sports grounds, roads
allBenefitsDescription: State-level equivalent of MPLADS. MLAs recommend development works in their constituency. Covers community halls, infrastructure, cultural spaces, and event venues.
benefitAmount: ₹1.5–₹3 crore per MLA per year (varies by state)
requiredDocuments: Project Proposal, Technical Estimate, Land Documents
remarks: Amount and rules vary state-to-state. Contact local MLA's office for details.

schemeName: Samagra Shiksha Abhiyan
department: Ministry of Education / Department of School Education & Literacy
targetGroup: School Students (Pre-primary to Class XII), Teachers, Govt Schools
eligibility: Students enrolled in government schools from pre-primary to Class XII; teachers and school administrators
otherEligibilityCriteria: Implemented via state government; individual benefits through government schools
benefits: School infrastructure funding; free uniforms, books, mid-day meals; learning events; community engagement; teacher training
allBenefitsDescription: Integrated scheme covering pre-school to senior secondary education. Funds school infrastructure, provides free textbooks and uniforms, supports mid-day meal programmes, and promotes inclusive quality education.
benefitAmount: Free uniforms, books; school infrastructure support (institutional)
requiredDocuments: Age proof, Address proof, Aadhaar, Caste Certificate (if applicable)
remarks: Merger of Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan, Rashtriya Madhyamik Shiksha Abhiyan, and Teacher Education.

schemeName: Ek Bharat Shreshtha Bharat
department: Ministry of Education
targetGroup: Students, Youth, Educational Institutions, Local Bodies
eligibility: Schools, colleges, local bodies, and cultural organizations organizing cultural exchange programs and awareness campaigns
otherEligibilityCriteria: Events focus on language, culture, cuisine, and traditions of paired states
benefits: Support for cultural events; awareness campaigns; state-pair exchange programs promoting national integration
allBenefitsDescription: Pairs states for cultural exchange to promote national unity. Funds cultural events, language learning, cuisine exchange, and youth exchange programs between paired states.
requiredDocuments: Institution ID, Event Plan, Participant List
remarks: Launched in 2015. Pairs states annually for cultural exchange activities.

schemeName: Mahila Shakti Kendra
department: Ministry of Women and Child Development
targetGroup: Women (especially rural), SHG members
eligibility: Rural and urban women; focuses on empowerment, skill training, and awareness
otherEligibilityCriteria: Implemented at block/district level
benefits: Skill training programs; health & legal awareness; community engagement; volunteer (SATHIN) network support
allBenefitsDescription: Provides one-stop convergence service for empowering rural women. Offers skill development, digital literacy, health awareness, legal aid, and connects women to government schemes.
requiredDocuments: Aadhaar Card, Address Proof, Photograph
remarks: Works through college student volunteers and community mobilizers.

schemeName: Stand-Up India Scheme
department: Department of Financial Services / SIDBI / NABARD
targetGroup: Women, SC/ST Entrepreneurs starting greenfield enterprises
eligibility: Women (any caste) or SC/ST (male/female); setting up greenfield enterprise; age 18+; not defaulter to any bank
otherEligibilityCriteria: At least one woman/SC/ST borrower per bank branch; greenfield project (first enterprise)
benefits: Composite bank loan ₹10 lakh to ₹1 crore; covers working capital and term loan; CGTMSE/NCGTC guarantee
allBenefitsDescription: Provides composite loans from ₹10 lakh to ₹1 crore for greenfield enterprises in manufacturing, services, or trading sectors. Covers both term loan and working capital. Repayment up to 7 years with moratorium.
importantDocuments: Aadhaar Card, PAN Card, Business Plan
requiredDocuments: Aadhaar Card, PAN Card, Business Plan/Project Report, Bank Account, Caste Certificate (for SC/ST), Address Proof
remarks: At least one SC/ST and one woman entrepreneur must be served per scheduled commercial bank branch.

schemeName: Metro Rail Policy 2017
department: Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs (MoHUA)
targetGroup: Urban residents in cities with metro population 2 million+
eligibility: Cities must prepare Comprehensive Mobility Plan (CMP); applicable for cities with population over 2 million
otherEligibilityCriteria: Requires UMTA (Unified Metropolitan Transport Authority) formation; alternative analysis mandatory
benefits: Central assistance up to 10–20% of project cost; PPP model support; multi-modal transport integration
allBenefitsDescription: Provides central grants/viability gap funding for metro rail projects. Mandates CMP, UMTA, last-mile connectivity integration. Promotes PPP models. Requires assessment of alternatives before metro approval.
benefitAmount: Up to 10–20% of project cost as central grant
requiredDocuments: Comprehensive Mobility Plan, Detailed Project Report, State Government resolution
remarks: Policy scheme; individual citizens benefit indirectly through improved urban transit.

schemeName: PRASHAD – Pilgrimage Rejuvenation and Spiritual Heritage Augmentation Drive
department: Ministry of Tourism
beneficiaryType: Pilgrimage Site Authorities / Local Bodies / Tourists
targetGroup: Religious tourists, pilgrims, ULBs near pilgrim sites
occupationEligible: ULBs, State Tourism Departments, Pilgrimage Site Managers
eligibility: Panchayats/municipalities near tourist/spiritual sites; state tourism departments; pilgrimage management bodies
otherEligibilityCriteria: Project proposals by state governments; must meet Ministry of Tourism guidelines
benefits: Funds roads, entry points, drinking water, toilets, lighting, CCTV, tourist facilities at pilgrim sites
allBenefitsDescription: Provides financial assistance for holistic development of identified pilgrim and spiritual tourism sites. Includes access roads, footpaths, amenities, safety systems, and visitor facilities.
applicationMode: State Government proposal to Ministry of Tourism
requiredDocuments: Detailed Project Report, State Government resolution, Site documents
remarks: Launched 2014-15. Benefits communities through employment and local economic growth.

schemeName: Swadesh Darshan 2.0
department: Ministry of Tourism
beneficiaryType: State Tourism Depts / Local Bodies / Tourism Stakeholders
targetGroup: Tourists, ULBs, Tourism entrepreneurs
occupationEligible: Tourism businesses, ULBs, State Tourism Departments
eligibility: State/UT tourism departments; destinations with potential for sustainable tourism development
otherEligibilityCriteria: Destination-centric approach; focus on eco-friendly and sustainable tourism
benefits: Funds parks, walkways, rural tourism hubs, eco-paths; promotes domestic tourism; PPP investment support
allBenefitsDescription: Upgraded from Swadesh Darshan 1.0. Promotes sustainable tourism destinations with focus on eco-tourism, culture, adventure, rural, and wellness themes. Funds both hard infrastructure and soft components.
applicationMode: State Government proposal to Ministry of Tourism
importantDocuments: Project DPR, State Tourism policy documents
requiredDocuments: DPR, State Govt resolution, Land documents
remarks: Upgraded version (2.0) from original 2014 scheme. Destination-centric, not circuit-based.

schemeName: Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana (PMGSY)
department: Ministry of Rural Development
targetGroup: Rural habitations without all-weather road connectivity
eligibility: Unconnected rural habitations with population 500+ (250+ in hill states); state rural roads agencies are implementing agencies
otherEligibilityCriteria: Road must be of public utility; single road connecting habitation to nearest all-weather route
benefits: Construction of all-weather roads; village street upgradation; connectivity to markets, schools, hospitals
allBenefitsDescription: Provides all-weather road connectivity to unconnected rural habitations. Includes new construction and upgrading of existing roads to meet standards. Also connects to markets, health centers, and educational institutions.
benefitAmount: Infrastructure benefit (no direct monetary benefit to individuals)
applicationMode: State Government / State Rural Roads Development Agency
requiredDocuments: Gram Panchayat resolution, Land documents, Technical estimates
remarks: Launched 2000. Over 7.5 lakh km of rural roads constructed. PMGSY-III (2019) focuses on upgradation.

schemeName: DAY-NRLM 2.0 – Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana – National Rural Livelihoods Mission
department: Ministry of Rural Development
targetGroup: Rural Poor Women, SHG Members, Rural Entrepreneurs
eligibility: Rural poor families identified via SECC; primarily targets women; organized into Self Help Groups
otherEligibilityCriteria: Must be willing to form/join SHG; household income below poverty line
benefits: SHG formation and capacity building; credit access via revolving funds; skill training; enterprise development; market linkage
allBenefitsDescription: NRLM 2.0 (2026-2031) focuses on creating high-income rural enterprises from SHGs. Provides revolving funds, credit linkage, skill development, digital inclusion, and market access. Targets financial independence for rural women.
benefitAmount: Revolving Fund ₹15,000 per SHG; Community Investment Fund up to ₹2.5 lakh per SHG
importantDocuments: Aadhaar Card, BPL Certificate, Bank Passbook
requiredDocuments: Aadhaar Card, BPL Certificate, SHG registration, Bank Account, Photograph
remarks: NRLM 2.0 formally transitions 2026-2031. 9 crore+ women mobilized in SHGs nationally.

schemeName: Swachh Bharat Mission – Urban (SBM-U 2.0)
department: Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs (MoHUA)
targetGroup: Urban households, waste workers, municipalities
eligibility: Urban households without toilet; ULBs for waste management infrastructure; BPL for toilet construction subsidy
otherEligibilityCriteria: Toilet subsidy for BPL households; waste management component for all urban areas
benefits: Toilet construction subsidy ₹12,000–₹14,000; solid waste management infrastructure; ODF++ certification support
allBenefitsDescription: SBM-U 2.0 (2021-2026) focuses on ODF sustainability, solid waste management, and wastewater treatment. Individual toilet subsidy ₹12,000-14,000 for BPL households. Also covers greywater management and plastic waste reduction.
importantDocuments: Aadhaar Card, BPL Certificate, Land/House Documents
requiredDocuments: Aadhaar Card, BPL Certificate, House ownership/rental proof, Bank Account
remarks: SBM-U 2.0 (2021-2026). Focus shifted from construction to sustainability and wastewater treatment.

schemeName: National Clean Air Programme (NCAP)
department: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC)
targetGroup: Residents of 107 non-attainment cities with high air pollution
eligibility: Indirect benefit; cities with PM2.5/PM10 above national standards; implemented by state/city pollution control boards
otherEligibilityCriteria: Policy scheme; funds urban air quality improvement measures
benefits: Reduction in PM2.5 and PM10 levels; improved air quality; funding for monitoring systems and pollution control measures
allBenefitsDescription: National programme to achieve 40% reduction in particulate matter by 2026. Funds air quality monitoring, EV adoption, industrial compliance, dust control, and public awareness in 107 polluted cities.
applicationMode: Implemented via State Pollution Control Boards / ULBs
requiredDocuments: N/A
remarks: Target: 40% reduction in PM levels by 2026. 131 cities covered (expanded from initial 102).

schemeName: FAME India Scheme Phase II (Faster Adoption and Manufacturing of EVs)
department: Ministry of Heavy Industries
targetGroup: Individual EV buyers, fleet operators, public transport authorities
occupationEligible: All EV buyers; fleet operators; public transport
eligibility: Buyers of eligible electric 2-wheelers, 3-wheelers, 4-wheelers, and buses meeting FAME-II criteria
otherEligibilityCriteria: Vehicle must meet localization requirements; purchased from FAME-II registered dealers
benefits: Upfront purchase subsidy on EVs; e-2W: up to ₹15,000; e-3W/buses: higher incentives; charging infrastructure support
allBenefitsDescription: Provides demand incentives for electric vehicles. E-2W: up to ₹15,000; e-3W taxis: up to ₹50,000; electric buses: up to ₹20 lakh. Also funds EV charging infrastructure in cities and highways.
applicationMode: Through EV dealer at point of sale
applicationDeadline: Ongoing (Phase III - PM E-Drive Scheme announced 2024)
requiredDocuments: Aadhaar Card, PAN Card, Bank Account, Vehicle Purchase Invoice
remarks: FAME II succeeded by PM E-DRIVE scheme in 2024 with ₹10,900 crore outlay. Check latest scheme.

schemeName: PM Surya Ghar – Rooftop Solar Programme (Grid Connected)
department: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE)
targetGroup: Residential households, Housing societies, RWAs
eligibility: Residential households with valid electricity connection and own rooftop space; RWAs for common area installation
otherEligibilityCriteria: Must install grid-connected system through DISCOM-approved vendor
benefits: Up to 40% subsidy on solar panel installation; free electricity up to 300 units/month; net metering credits
allBenefitsDescription: PM Surya Ghar (launched 2024): up to 40% subsidy for 1-2 kW systems, 20% for 2-3 kW. Target 1 crore households. Provides free electricity (up to 300 units/month) and income from surplus solar power via net metering.
importantDocuments: Electricity Bill, Aadhaar Card, Property Documents
requiredDocuments: Electricity bill, Aadhaar Card, Bank Account, Property ownership proof, Photograph
remarks: Rebranded from Rooftop Solar Phase II to PM Surya Ghar in 2024. Target: 1 crore installations.

schemeName: AMRUT 2.0 – Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation
department: Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs (MoHUA)
targetGroup: Urban households, residents of 500 cities
eligibility: Residents of 500 AMRUT cities; ULBs implement projects; individual benefit via improved infrastructure
otherEligibilityCriteria: AMRUT 2.0 focuses on water security – 100% tap connections to all households
benefitType: Infrastructure / Water Supply / Sanitation / Green Spaces
benefits: Water supply connections; sewerage networks; green spaces and parks; urban mobility improvement
allBenefitsDescription: AMRUT 2.0 (2021-2026) aims for water security in 4,700+ cities. Provides 100% household tap water connections, sewerage networks, septage management, and urban green space development including parks.
benefitAmount: Infrastructure benefit (₹2.99 lakh crore mission outlay)
requiredDocuments: ULB project proposal, DPR, land documents
remarks: AMRUT 2.0 covers 4,700+ cities vs AMRUT 1.0's 500 cities. Includes parks and open spaces.

schemeName: Smart Cities Mission
department: Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs (MoHUA)
targetGroup: Residents of 100 selected smart cities
eligibility: Residents of 100 selected smart cities; projects implemented by Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV)
otherEligibilityCriteria: City selection through competitive challenge process; ₹500 crore central funding per city
benefits: Smart waste management; green mobility; energy-efficient buildings; public Wi-Fi; Integrated Command Control Centers
allBenefitsDescription: Provides ₹500 crore per selected city for Area-Based Development and Pan-City initiatives. Covers smart solutions like ICCCs, smart roads, solar energy, cycling infrastructure, and digital citizen services.
requiredDocuments: Smart City Proposal, SPV documents
remarks: 100 cities selected. Mission extended to 2025. Focus on area-based and pan-city improvements.

schemeName: Plastic Waste Management Initiative (Plastic Waste Management Rules 2016/2022)
department: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC)
targetGroup: All citizens, manufacturers, importers, brand owners
eligibility: All citizens and businesses; mandatory compliance for manufacturers, importers, brand owners of plastic items
otherEligibilityCriteria: Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) mandatory for plastic producers
benefits: Ban on single-use plastics (effective 2022); EPR framework; recycling promotion; waste collection systems
allBenefitsDescription: Bans 19 categories of single-use plastic items from July 2022. Mandates Extended Producer Responsibility for plastic manufacturers. Promotes plastic waste segregation, collection, and recycling at ULB level.
requiredDocuments: Business registration, CPCB EPR registration
remarks: Single-use plastic ban effective July 2022. EPR framework mandatory for producers.

schemeName: Nagar Van Yojana (Urban Green Spaces / City Forest Scheme)
department: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC)
targetGroup: Urban communities, municipal corporations, civic bodies
eligibility: Municipal corporations, urban local bodies, NGOs, RWAs proposing city forest/green space projects; minimum 10 hectare land available
otherEligibilityCriteria: Must have identified land; project proposal to State Forest Department
benefits: Development of city forests; biodiversity parks; urban green spaces; ecological restoration of urban land
allBenefitsDescription: Creates Nagar Vans (city forests) across urban India. Provides technical and financial support for developing green spaces, biodiversity parks, and ecological areas in cities. Target: 200 city forests.
requiredDocuments: Land ownership/clearance, Project DPR, Municipal resolution
remarks: Target: 200 Nagar Vans by 2024. NGOs and RWAs can partner with municipalities.

schemeName: Energy Conservation Building Code (ECBC) Implementation
department: Bureau of Energy Efficiency (BEE), Ministry of Power
targetGroup: Commercial buildings >500 sqm, government buildings, architects, builders
eligibility: New commercial buildings above 500 sqm; mandatory for government buildings; ECBC+ and super-ECBC for higher efficiency
otherEligibilityCriteria: States must adopt ECBC in building byelaws; currently mandatory in ~25 states
benefits: 25–50% energy savings in buildings; green building certification; ECO Niwas Samhita for residential
allBenefitsDescription: Mandates energy-efficient building design for commercial buildings. ECBC compliance results in 25-50% energy savings. ECO Niwas Samhita (residential ECBC) promotes energy efficiency in homes. BEE provides technical support.
benefitAmount: Energy cost savings (₹2–4 lakh/year for typical commercial building)
applicationMode: Through building permit process / State Building Authority
requiredDocuments: Building plans, Energy audit report, Architect certification
remarks: Mandatory for commercial buildings >500 sqm in states that have adopted ECBC.

schemeName: National Mission for Green India (Green India Mission)
department: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC)
beneficiaryType: State Forest Depts / Local Communities / NGOs
targetGroup: Communities near forests, tribal communities, NGOs, forest departments
eligibility: State forest departments, tribal communities, and NGOs; focus on degraded forests and non-forest ecosystems
otherEligibilityCriteria: Target: increase forest/tree cover by 5 million hectares
benefits: Funding for afforestation; urban greening; eco-restoration; community livelihood through forest-based activities
allBenefitsDescription: Aims to increase forest/tree cover by 5 million hectares. Provides funding for afforestation of degraded forests, grasslands, and urban areas. Supports community forest management and ecosystem service enhancement.
requiredDocuments: Project DPR, Land records, Community resolution
remarks: One of India's 8 National Action Plan on Climate Change missions.

schemeName: CAMPA – Compensatory Afforestation Fund Management and Planning Authority
department: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC)
beneficiaryType: State Forest Departments / Local Gram Panchayats
targetGroup: Forest-dependent communities, tribal populations
eligibility: State forest departments submit afforestation proposals; funds from entities diverting forest land for non-forest use
otherEligibilityCriteria: 70% funds to states; 30% to central; only for afforestation and forest management activities
benefits: Funding for compensatory afforestation; assisted natural regeneration; forest protection; wildlife management
allBenefitsDescription: Manages funds collected as compensation when forest land is diverted. Funds tree plantation, forest management, eco-restoration, and livelihood activities in forest areas. ₹60,000+ crore corpus.
requiredDocuments: Afforestation proposal, Land documents
remarks: CAMPA Act 2016. Funds compensatory afforestation when forests are diverted for development projects.

schemeName: Khelo India Scheme (Khelo India Youth Games)
department: Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
targetGroup: School children (5–18), Athletes, Sports Academies, Physical education teachers
eligibility: Young athletes up to 18–21 years; schools and sports institutions; talented athletes from rural/semi-urban areas
otherEligibilityCriteria: Khelo India Athletes (KIA) receive ₹6.28 lakh/year scholarship for 8 years; selection via competition
benefits: Annual scholarship ₹6.28 lakh for selected athletes; sports infrastructure development at grassroots; coaching support; mass participation programs
allBenefitsDescription: Promotes mass participation in sports and identifies talent at school level. Provides ₹6.28 lakh/year scholarship to Khelo India Athletes for 8 years. Funds playground renovation, sports equipment, and Small Centres of Excellence.
applicationMode: Online (kheloindia.gov.in) / Through schools and sports bodies
importantDocuments: Aadhaar Card, Age proof, Sports achievement certificates
requiredDocuments: Aadhaar Card, Age proof, Passport photo, Sports certificates, School ID
remarks: KIYG (Youth Games) and KIUG (University Games) held annually. Covers 26 sports disciplines.

schemeName: Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana – Urban (PMAY-U 2.0)
department: Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs (MoHUA)
targetGroup: Economically Weaker Section (EWS), Low Income Group (LIG), Middle Income Group (MIG)
incomeLimit: EWS: up to ₹3 lakh/year; LIG: ₹3–6 lakh; MIG-I: ₹6–12 lakh; MIG-II: ₹12–18 lakh
eligibility: Must not own a pucca house anywhere in India; family must not have availed central housing scheme before; must be urban resident
otherEligibilityCriteria: EWS/LIG: in-situ slum rehabilitation or beneficiary-led construction; MIG: credit-linked subsidy on home loans
benefits: Interest subsidy on home loan (CLSS); direct subsidy for house construction; in-situ slum rehabilitation
allBenefitsDescription: PMAY-U 2.0 (2024-2029) targets 1 crore urban poor with pucca houses. Provides Central Assistance of ₹1.5 lakh (EWS/LIG), ₹1.8 lakh (MIG). Credit Linked Subsidy Scheme (CLSS) offers subsidy on home loans.
benefitAmount: EWS/LIG: ₹1.5 lakh subsidy; MIG: ₹1.8 lakh subsidy; CLSS: ₹2.35–2.67 lakh interest subsidy
importantDocuments: Aadhaar Card, Income Certificate, No property ownership certificate
requiredDocuments: Aadhaar Card, Income certificate, Address proof, Bank account, Property documents (if applicable), Photograph
remarks: Female co-ownership mandatory for EWS/LIG. Must not own pucca house in India. PMAY-U 2.0 launched 2024.

schemeName: Mahatma Jyotiba Phule Jan Arogya Yojana (MJPJAY) – Maharashtra
department: Government of Maharashtra / Department of Public Health
beneficiaryType: BPL / Yellow Ration Card Holders / Farmers (Maharashtra)
targetGroup: BPL families, Yellow/Orange ration card holders, farmers in debt
incomeLimit: Yellow/Orange ration card holders; also white card in some cases
eligibility: Maharashtra resident; Yellow/Orange ration card holder; BPL or low-income family; farmers under agriculture loan distress
otherEligibilityCriteria: Coverage extends to include Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY beneficiaries in Maharashtra
benefits: ₹5 lakh health coverage per family per year; 1,000+ medical procedures covered; cashless treatment at empanelled hospitals
allBenefitsDescription: State scheme providing ₹5 lakh cashless health coverage for 996+ procedures. Covers BPL families with Yellow/Orange ration cards. Recently extended to White ration card holders in some districts. Integrated with Ayushman Bharat.
benefitAmount: Up to ₹5,00,000 per family per year
importantDocuments: Ration Card (Yellow/Orange), Aadhaar Card, Maharashtra domicile
requiredDocuments: Aadhaar Card, Ration Card, Maharashtra Domicile Certificate, Bank Account
remarks: Maharashtra-specific scheme. Also covers debt-distressed farmers' families. Integrated with Ayushman Bharat.

schemeName: Skill India Mission (National Skill Development Mission)
department: Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE) / NSDC

remarks: Mission launched 2015. Houses PMKVY, NAPS, and other skill programs as sub-components.

schemeName: Delhi Free Bus Travel for Women Scheme
department: Government of Delhi / Delhi Transport Corporation (DTC)

eligibility: Any woman traveling in Delhi in DTC/cluster buses; simply board the bus and request pink ticket
otherEligibilityCriteria: Valid in DTC and cluster buses only; not applicable for Metro
benefits: Free unlimited travel in DTC and cluster buses; pink ticket issued at no cost
allBenefitsDescription: Women can travel free in all Delhi DTC and cluster buses by requesting a 'pink ticket' at no charge. Scheme launched October 2019 to ensure safe and affordable mobility for women in Delhi.

requiredDocuments: No documents required; just board the bus
remarks: Launched October 2019. Applicable in DTC and cluster buses only. Not valid for Delhi Metro.
